page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.2xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, providing a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A key hardware characteristic is the inclusion of 23,622 GB of local HDD storage, offering massive storage capacity directly attached to the instance. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals clear performance tradeoffs for this instance type. The CPU performance is generally modest, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core benchmarks scoring in the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 10% tier. Memory performance is also constrained, as indicated by a weak PassMark memory score and a weak read-only large-block memory bandwidth of 37.11 GB/sec, though large-block write bandwidth achieves an average rating at 34.88 GB/sec. PassMark CPU and extended instruction tests score in the average tier, but database operations and Redis SET operations remain in the bottom 25% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.d1.2xlarge offers high local storage density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads requiring massive data capacity without demanding high-performance processing. However, the reliance on HDD storage and the weak CPU and memory benchmarks represent a significant tradeoff for latency-sensitive applications. This instance is best suited for cold data storage, large-scale log archiving, data warehousing, and batch processing workloads where storage volume is prioritized over high-speed computational throughput or rapid random I/O.
